clue.text: Woman twirling favourite slip

parts.note: a miss is a young woman

indicators.note: something twirling is turned round, so the word for favourite is read the other way

parts.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A woman spinning round in her favourite slip, the undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A misstep is a stumble or error, just as a slip is a small mistake or loss of footing.

clue.text: Glibness might result from this combination of positive and negative qualities

definitions.text: combination of positive and negative qualities

indicators.note: the clue word is what might come out of the answer read as an instruction, so the instruction is worked backwards

parts.note: 'this' points to the answer itself, whose first word is the mixing instruction
the letters a mixed version of the answer's second word would produce

explanation.surface: Smooth talk might come from having both good and bad qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse anagram: read the answer as an instruction, 'BLESSING, mixed', and its letters can give GLIBNESS. The word MIXED is the instruction itself, so no clue word supplies it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed blessing is something with both advantages and drawbacks.

clue.text: Important military incursion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: most noticeable or significant
second meaning: a bulge of a battle line pushing into enemy territory

explanation.surface: A significant military raid.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient points are the prominent ones, and in warfare a salient is a forward bulge of the front into enemy ground.

clue.text: Use fast filling snacks

parts.note: to tap a resource is to use it

indicators.note: the filling of a word is its inside, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of fast

explanation.surface: Eat a quick bite of filling snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filling' looks like an adjective for satisfying food; it is the instruction to take the inside of 'fast'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small Spanish dishes served as snacks with drinks.

clue.text: Charges after deleting former lover's letters

definitions.note: plosives are consonant sounds, here taken as the letters representing them

indicators.note: deleting removes letters, here the word for a former partner

parts.note: explosive charges, as in demolition
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Charges brought after someone deleted their ex's letters, a messy break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like correspondence; it means letters of the alphabet such as P, B, T, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Plosives are consonants like P and B made by stopping and then releasing the breath.

clue.text: Reason 2 down's entered

indicators.note: something entered goes inside, so the down abbreviation sits within the word for two

parts.note: a deuce is a two in cards or dice
D is the standard abbreviation for down

explanation.surface: A cross-reference asking the solver to work out why 2 Down has been entered in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The '2 down' looks like a pointer to another clue, but the 2 is read as a number and 'down' as an abbreviation: D goes into DEUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce is to reach a conclusion by logical thought, which is what the verb reason means.

clue.text: Tempted to backtrack with advancing death

indicators.note: advancing means moving forward, so the death letter at the back goes to the front

parts.note: to rewind a tape is to go back over it

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to turn back as death approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: D, short for dead or died, here stands for death; it is already the last letter of REWIND and moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw someone in is to lure or entice them, so drew in means tempted.

clue.text: Compulsory EU rights guide revised

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right, here plural so two of them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A revised guide to EU rights is now mandatory reading.
explanation.definitionFit: De rigueur, borrowed from French, means required by etiquette or fashion, so obligatory.

clue.text: Toast a half-dead farce

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: to char is to scorch, as when toasting
taken as written
taken as written, then halved

explanation.surface: Raising a glass to a half-dead comedy, a theatrical flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' reads as a drink's salute; it is the verb, to scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence, the sense of farce as an empty sham.

clue.text: Axes chop end off precious musical instrument

indicators.note: with its end off, a word loses its final letter

parts.note: x and y are the two axes of a graph
to lop is to chop off
precious and honey are both terms of endearment

explanation.surface: Axes hacking the end off something valuable, a scene of destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precious' reads as an adjective for something valuable, but it is the endearment, like darling or honey, which loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A xylophone is a percussion instrument of tuned wooden bars struck with mallets.

clue.text: Authentic capital of magic kingdom

parts.note: real means genuine or authentic

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its initial, upper-case letter

parts.note: first letter of magic

explanation.surface: The genuine capital city of some magic kingdom, as in a fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, the territory a monarch rules.

clue.text: Mass spectrometer's introduction succeeds as much as test configuration

indicators.note: a configuration is an arrangement, so the letters are put in a new order
the introduction of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of spectrometer
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A mass spectrometer's debut proves as good as the test setup, a lab report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks part of 'mass spectrometer'; it is Mass., the standard US abbreviation for the state, and 'succeeds' just places S before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass. is the postal-style abbreviation of Massachusetts, the New England state.

clue.text: Grounds for registration being taken by police officer

indicators.note: what is taken by someone is held, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: DS is a detective sergeant
reg is the usual short form of registration, as on a car

explanation.surface: A justification for a vehicle registration being confiscated by a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' looks like reasons, matching the legal surface, but it means coffee grounds, the sediment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are the sediment left at the bottom of a drink, like coffee grounds.

clue.text: Revolution beheaded female agent for making things clear

indicators.note: beheading removes the head, the first letter of the word

parts.note: a rising is a revolt or revolution
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A revolution that executed a female spy, for reasons left unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female agent' reads as a spy, but the definition is the whole tail, 'agent for making things clear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is a fish gelatine used as a fining substance to clarify beer and wine.

clue.text: Had babies strewn about

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gave birth to a brood of young animals
second meaning: scattered untidily with rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone had babies and things are scattered everywhere, a picture of chaotic family life.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that has a litter of young has littered, and a floor covered in scattered mess is littered.

clue.text: Girl supports end of cake decoration

indicators.note: in a down entry, what supports something sits below it
the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of cake
Paulette is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl holds up the last of the cake decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cake decoration' looks like one phrase; the definition is 'decoration' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulette is an ornamental shoulder piece on a uniform, a decoration worn on the shoulder.

clue.text: What is inherited by Virginia's lakeside city

parts.note: genes are the units of heredity
VA is the US abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: Someone inheriting property in Virginia, with a city on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is the Swiss city on the shore of Lake Geneva.

clue.text: Manifesto format manipulated by political extremes

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, placed alongside

parts.note: first and last letters of political

indicators.note: manipulated material is handled and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A party manifesto whose format has been spun by political extremists.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's platform is its declared set of policies, which is what a manifesto sets out.

clue.text: Sorcerer's not genuine article

parts.note: a sham is a fake
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A sorcerer is not the genuine article, a fraud exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not genuine article' reads as one phrase meaning a fake; it splits into the fake and the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a healer or priest believed to wield magic, in effect a sorcerer.

clue.text: Bleak House's climax adopted by American writer

indicators.note: adopted by means taken on by the writer, attached at his end

parts.note: Paul Auster was an American novelist

indicators.note: the climax comes at the end, so take the last letter

parts.note: last letter of house

explanation.surface: The ending of Dickens's Bleak House taken over by an American novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bleak House' looks like the Dickens title, but 'Bleak' is the definition and 'House' just supplies its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means stark and plain, without comfort, which is a sense of bleak.

clue.text: Spooky tale's opening welcomed by unruly children — but not ending

indicators.note: one welcomed by others is taken in among them, so a letter goes inside
unruly children are disorderly, so the letters are put in disorder
not ending means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of tale

explanation.surface: Unruly children welcoming a ghost story's start, but the story never finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Eldritch is a Scots-origin word for weird, unearthly and eerie, a synonym of spooky.

clue.text: Hybrid take over's leading characters include investor

indicators.note: to include is to hold inside, so the investor goes between the letters
the leading characters of words are their first letters

parts.note: first letters of take and over
an angel is a backer who invests in a show or start-up

explanation.surface: A takeover bid by an investor, in the jargon of corporate finance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hybrid' sounds like a business structure; it is a fruit cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus fruit bred by crossing a tangerine with a pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: Drill more off?

parts.note: less is the opposite of more
on is the opposite of off

explanation.surface: Asking whether more drilling should be switched off.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word gives its opposite rather than a synonym, and the question mark flags that unusual step.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a repeated exercise for teaching, and a lesson is a period of instruction.

clue.text: Bust make up is worn by half of you

indicators.note: something worn is wrapped around the wearer, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to make up a story is to invent it

indicators.note: half of a word keeps only three of its six letters

parts.note: in a crossword, you the reader are the solver

explanation.surface: Bust make-up worn by half of you, a cosmetics tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust make up' looks like cosmetics for the chest; bust means broke, and 'you' is the crossword solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bust has gone bankrupt, unable to pay debts, which is insolvent.

clue.text: Fetishes are known to start with tattoos

indicators.note: to start means use only the opening letter of the word

parts.note: first letter of known
to ink someone is to tattoo them

explanation.surface: Kinks are famously begun with tattoos, a remark about body art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' simply places the tattoo word after the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A kink is an unusual sexual preference, much the same as a fetish.

clue.text: Glory for solving unfinished su doku

indicators.note: solving a puzzle means working its pieces into order, so the letters are rearranged
unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: Praise for finishing a sudoku, even one left incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is praise and honour earned by an achievement, a near synonym of glory.

clue.text: Caught suspected intruder — not at all!

indicators.note: to catch a remark is to hear it, so the word is taken by sound

parts.note: suspected means guessed, which sounds the same as the answer

explanation.surface: Someone caught a suspected intruder, only to be told it was nothing of the kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic twist: someone in the house who is the opposite of an intruder, because they were invited.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is a visitor who has been invited, so is precisely not an intruder.

clue.text: Most grotty dishes do get smashed ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of places the jumbled letters before the time abbreviation
smashed crockery is broken into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The scruffiest crockery gets broken before its time.
explanation.walkthrough: Grotty is British slang for unpleasant or of poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy means badly made or poor quality, so the shoddiest thing is the most grotty.

clue.text: Humiliate compiler in article following editor's rejection

indicators.note: following puts the compiler-and-article unit after the rejected editor
a rejected thing is sent back, so the editor's abbreviation is read backwards
in places the compiler alongside the article, the two forming one unit

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor
the compiler is the setter, who refers to themselves as me
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A setter humiliated by having their article rejected by the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves 'me'; 'in' is loose here, since the compiler simply stands before the article rather than inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity, which is to humiliate them.

clue.text: Talismans include manger in a Christian service

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic eucharistic service
a manger served as the baby Jesus's cot

explanation.surface: Lucky charms featuring a manger in a Christmas church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascots are objects or creatures kept to bring good luck, as talismans are.
